topStories.headline: SoMa at a Crossroads: Fifth Street Splits a Neighborhood Between Boom and Bust
topStories.dek: An SF Standard investigation published September 3 finds AI-fueled revival east of Fifth Street running headlong into lingering pandemic-era emptiness to the west — one neighborhood, two entirely different realities.
topStories.body:
South of Market is simultaneously San Francisco's hottest recovery story and one of its deepest open wounds, according to a major investigation published September 3 by the SF Standard. The piece opens at 415 Natoma — a 25-story glass-and-steel tower at Fifth and Mission streets that is gleamingly modern yet almost entirely vacant — and uses it to frame the neighborhood's unresolved contradictions. Fifth Street, the Standard reports, has become SoMa's unofficial dividing line: east of it, large office leases are being signed, condos are selling after years of stagnation, and the Moscone Center's conference calendar is full; west of it, the neighborhood still feels like a time capsule from the depths of the pandemic.

Broader market data backs up the split picture. A Q2 2026 office market report published in mid-August by Hughes Marino found that San Francisco tenants leased 2.8 million square feet in the second quarter alone, bringing year-to-date leasing to 7 million square feet — with citywide vacancy falling roughly 5 percentage points year-over-year to about 29.7 percent, described as the fastest decline of any major U.S. market. Artificial intelligence companies remain the engine of the recovery, with Showplace Square on SoMa's southern edge emerging as a hub for AI and robotics tenants.

But the gains are sharply uneven building by building. The 415 Natoma tower — a 650,000-square-foot Class A property that opened in 2022 — changed hands in April after Brookfield's lender took a loss, with Meridian Group and Fenway Capital Advisors completing an ownership transfer through a discounted deed-in-lieu-of-foreclosure transaction. Properties like it, which opened into the weakest office market in a generation, still account for a disproportionate share of available space even as well-positioned, renovated buildings absorb new tenants.

The SF Standard describes SoMa as the place where San Francisco rises higher and falls harder than anywhere else. The neighborhood's split condition is more than a real estate story: it reflects how differently recovery lands on residents, small businesses, and service workers depending on which side of a single street they occupy — and it will do much to shape the city's broader fiscal outlook in the years ahead.

topStories.headline: Mission Bay Elementary Is Now in Session — SF's First New Public School in 20 Years Navigates Its Opening Weeks
topStories.dek: The ribbon was cut August 6 and the first students arrived August 17; as September begins, the neighborhood's long-awaited school is in the thick of its inaugural weeks.
topStories.body:
Mission Bay Elementary School celebrated its grand opening on August 6, 2026, with Principal Monette Benitez cutting the ribbon before city leaders, families, and educators. The school welcomed its inaugural class — pre-kindergarten through kindergarten — on August 17, and is now in its first full weeks of the 2026-27 school year. It is the first new San Francisco Unified School District school to open in 20 years and the first public school campus ever built in the Mission Bay neighborhood.

The four-story building at 1415 Owens Street was funded by San Francisco's 2016 Proposition A bond measure and will initially serve pre-K through kindergarten, expanding one grade at a time until it reaches full TK-through-5 enrollment of more than 400 students by 2032. The fourth floor houses the Mission Bay Hub, a STEM career-pathway program drawing high school students from six schools citywide. The interior design centers on what architect Chris McGiff-Brown calls 'Universal Design for Learning' — wide, movable glass doors that allow classrooms and workspaces to be combined or reconfigured.

The school responds to a long-documented need. Mission Bay's population has nearly doubled over the past 15 years, but families there — along with those in SoMa, Potrero Hill, and Dogpatch — have historically faced some of the district's most competitive enrollment conditions, with no attendance-area school nearby. SFUSD has called the project the product of more than two decades of planning and community input, integral to rapid housing development along the city's east side.

The opening arrives in the same SFUSD cycle in which the district is consolidating campuses elsewhere in response to declining citywide enrollment — making Mission Bay an unusual new chapter in a system that is, in most other places, contracting rather than growing.

topStories.headline: Ten Candidates, One Open Seat: District 10 Supervisor Race Heads Into Its Final Stretch
topStories.dek: With term-limited Shamann Walton departing, a crowded November ballot is taking shape for the district covering Potrero Hill, Dogpatch, Bayview-Hunters Point, and the central waterfront.
topStories.body:
Supervisor Shamann Walton will leave San Francisco's District 10 seat after two terms, setting off one of the most closely watched supervisor races on the November 2026 ballot. Ten candidates have qualified, competing to represent a district that stretches roughly from Potrero Hill and Dogpatch south through Bayview-Hunters Point, Candlestick Point, and Visitacion Valley — encompassing some of the city's fastest-changing waterfront territory alongside some of its most historically underserved communities.

Three candidates have emerged as the frontrunners: Theo Ellington, Dion-Jay Brookter, and J.R. Eppler. Ellington secured the San Francisco Democratic Party's sole endorsement for D10 in July 2026 and is backed by a broad coalition of moderate and establishment supporters, including state officials, former mayors, and major labor unions. Brookter followed Walton as executive director of Young Community Developers and has emphasized his deep community ties in the district. Eppler, a Potrero Hill attorney who has lived in the neighborhood since 2010, has been endorsed by civic leaders including the executive director of the Dogpatch and Potrero Hill Green Benefit District.

The Potrero View, which has covered Potrero Hill, Dogpatch, Mission Bay, and SoMa since 1970, ran a multi-part Q&A series with the leading candidates in its April, May, and July 2026 issues. Issues at the center of the race include housing affordability, public safety, and oversight of large-scale waterfront development projects at Pier 70 and the Potrero Power Station site, which together represent thousands of planned new homes and acres of public open space.

San Francisco uses ranked-choice voting for Board of Supervisors elections. The winner will inherit a district undergoing rapid and uneven transformation — with new demographics arriving in Dogpatch and Mission Bay and longtime Bayview-Hunters Point residents watching closely whether the benefits of that growth reach them.

events.description: SFMOMA's exclusive exhibition on Matisse's 1905 painting — more than 90 works tracing its scandalous debut and lasting influence on art history — closes September 13. Members can attend special Last Looks sessions September 12–13 from 10 a.m. to noon.

moreNews.headline: SF Parking Tickets Rose 21 Percent From December to May, Per Potrero View's August Report
moreNews.body: The Potrero View's August 2026 issue flagged a significant spike in city parking enforcement: citing data from the SF Standard, the paper reported that total parking tickets issued in San Francisco rose 21 percent between December 2025 and May 2026. The surge was noted as a concern for residents and small businesses in Potrero Hill, Dogpatch, and SoMa. No official explanation from the city has been published for the increase.

moreNews.headline: Potrero Power Station's UCSF Cancer Research Block Has Foundation Underway; Broader Project Seeks Entitlement Changes
moreNews.body: Foundation work was reported as underway in February 2026 on Block 2 of the Potrero Power Station redevelopment in Dogpatch — a seven-story UCSF cancer research center designed by Herzog & de Meuron, per SF YIMBY. The site's adjacent Sophie Maxwell Building, 105 units of permanently affordable housing, opened in October 2025. In July 2026, the SF Chronicle reported that developer Fifth Space (formerly Associate Capital) has sought modifications to the project's entitlements to improve financial feasibility — a move the Chronicle noted several other major San Francisco developments have made since the pandemic. The full Potrero Power Station plan calls for more than 2,600 homes and nearly 7 acres of open space on a former waterfront power plant site closed to the public for roughly 150 years.

restaurants.description: The annexed cocktail bar next door to Piccino, specializing in classic craft cocktails and small bites in a laidback setting.

restaurants.name: Sightglass Coffee (SoMa Flagship)
restaurants.description: Sightglass's bi-level SoMa flagship houses the company's roastery, open coffee bar, headquarters, and a Friday public cupping lab where guests can taste freshly roasted single-origin coffees.

restaurants.name: SPARK Social SF
restaurants.type: Outdoor food truck park and beer garden
restaurants.description: Mission Bay's open-air food truck park features a rotating lineup of over a dozen trucks daily, a beer and sangria garden, fire pits, and an 18-hole mini golf course, drawing a crowd of UCSF staff, tech workers, and families.
restaurants.address: 601 Mission Bay Blvd N, San Francisco, CA 94158

restaurants.name: Mersea Restaurant
restaurants.description: Situated on Treasure Island with panoramic Bay views, Mersea serves American coastal cuisine and craft cocktails, and hosts free live music on Fridays, Saturdays, and Sundays.
restaurants.address: 1 Avenue of the Palms, Treasure Island, San Francisco, CA 94130

restaurants.name: Gold Bar Whiskey Distillery
restaurants.type: Craft spirits distillery and tasting room
restaurants.description: Set inside a 1930s Art Deco building on Treasure Island, Gold Bar offers whiskey flights, signature cocktails, and sweeping views of the San Francisco skyline, with live jazz on weekend evenings.
restaurants.address: Avenue of the Palms, Treasure Island, San Francisco, CA 94130

restaurants.name: Besharam
restaurants.description: Chef Heena Patel's bold, vegetable-forward Indian restaurant at the Minnesota Street Project celebrates the bold flavors of Gujarat and is a community fixture at the Dogpatch arts campus.

restaurants.name: Cafe Alma
restaurants.description: A beloved Potrero Hill corner café serving breakfast, brunch, and coffee with a warm neighborhood-gathering-place feel.

restaurants.name: Anchor Public Taps
restaurants.description: The taproom for San Francisco's legendary Anchor Brewing Company, pouring a full range of Anchor beers alongside brewery tours in a spacious SoMa setting.
restaurants.address: 495 De Haro St, San Francisco, CA 94107

restaurants.name: Plow
restaurants.description: A long-running Potrero Hill favorite known for its ricotta pancakes, farm egg scrambles, and weekend lines — one of the city's definitive brunch destinations.

restaurants.name: Chez Maman
restaurants.description: A charming, unpretentious French bistro on Potrero Hill serving crêpes, moules frites, and classic Gallic comfort food in a cozy setting.

restaurants.name: Dogpatch Saloon
restaurants.description: A casual, unpretentious dive bar and neighborhood anchor in Dogpatch with cold beer, sports on TV, and a loyal local following.

restaurants.name: Smokestack at Magnolia Brewing
restaurants.description: Magnolia Brewing's Dogpatch location combines a working brewery and taproom with a full barbecue menu of smoked meats and classic sides in a large industrial space.

restaurants.name: Bloodhound
restaurants.description: A well-regarded SoMa cocktail bar with an extensive whiskey list, craft cocktails, and a hunter's-lodge aesthetic that draws a stylish after-work crowd.

restaurants.name: El Río
restaurants.description: A beloved, longstanding SoMa bar with a shaded backyard patio, Latin-tinged programming, and a proud LGBTQ+ welcoming tradition since 1978.

restaurants.name: The Bird SF
restaurants.description: A popular quick-service spot in SoMa known for its fried chicken sandwiches on housemade biscuits and chipotle-ranch sauce, serving a brisk lunch crowd near Moscone Center.
restaurants.address: 115 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA 94105

restaurants.name: Luce at InterContinental San Francisco
restaurants.description: The upscale restaurant inside the InterContinental San Francisco holds a Michelin star and serves Californian cuisine with Mediterranean influences in an elegant SoMa setting.

restaurants.name: Brenda's Meat & Three
restaurants.description: Chef Brenda Buenviaje's SoMa outpost offers classic Southern plates — fried chicken, catfish, and rotating vegetable sides — in a casual, counter-service format.

hotels.name: InterContinental San Francisco by IHG
hotels.description: A 32-story glass tower directly adjacent to Moscone Center offering 554 rooms, a Michelin-starred restaurant, an indoor pool, and panoramic Bay Area views — the 2026 Best of the Bay winner for Best Hotel for Business.

hotels.name: Hotel VIA
hotels.description: A stylish boutique hotel steps from Oracle Park and Chase Center in Mission Bay, featuring a rooftop bar with sweeping Bay views, a well-equipped gym, and a guest rating of 9.2 out of 10.

hotels.name: LUMA Hotel San Francisco
hotels.description: A contemporary hotel in Mission Bay near UCSF offering modern rooms, flexible meeting spaces, and easy access to Chase Center and the waterfront.
hotels.address: 55 Cyril Magnin St, San Francisco, CA 94102

hotels.name: Hyatt Place San Francisco Downtown
hotels.description: A 230-room hotel in SoMa offering oversized rooms, a rooftop bar with city views, and a central location within walking distance of Moscone Center, SFMOMA, and the Caltrain station.

hotels.name: Canopy by Hilton San Francisco SoMa
hotels.description: A design-forward Hilton lifestyle brand property in SoMa, praised for its welcoming atmosphere and proximity to Yerba Buena Gardens and public transit.

hotels.name: W San Francisco
hotels.description: The W brand's San Francisco flagship brings bold design and a lively bar scene to SoMa, located within walking distance of SFMOMA and Yerba Buena Gardens.

hotels.name: San Francisco Proper Hotel
hotels.description: A Kelly Wearstler–designed boutique property at the edge of the Tenderloin and SoMa, featuring a rooftop bar, a Michelin-recognized restaurant, and richly layered interiors.

hotels.name: YOTEL San Francisco
hotels.description: A smartly designed tech-forward hotel with compact, efficiently laid-out cabins, a rooftop bar, and a playful aesthetic aimed at modern travelers near Moscone Center.

shops.name: Minnesota Street Project Shop
shops.description: The retail arm of the Dogpatch arts campus sells limited-edition prints, artist books, and art objects from galleries and artists in residence at Minnesota Street Project.

shops.name: DIG Wine
shops.description: A curated natural and boutique wine shop inside Dogpatch's Yellow Building, known for its knowledgeable staff and selections that pair well with a visit to neighboring Piccino.

shops.name: Rickshaw Bagworks
shops.description: A San Francisco–made bag manufacturer and retail shop on 22nd Street in Dogpatch, offering messenger bags, laptop sleeves, and custom bags produced in the neighborhood.

shops.name: Paxton Gate
shops.description: An only-in-San-Francisco shop selling taxidermy, fossils, exotic plants, terrariums, and scientific oddities that has been a SoMa landmark for decades.

shops.name: 826 Valencia (Pirate Supply Store)
shops.type: Nonprofit writing center with pirate supply storefront
shops.description: Dave Eggers's beloved nonprofit tutoring center for young writers disguises its entrance as a legitimate purveyor of pirate supplies, with the profits supporting free youth writing programs.

shops.name: Heath Ceramics
shops.description: The flagship studio and retail shop of Heath Ceramics on Utah Street in Potrero Hill offers the full range of the California-made ceramic tableware brand, with a manufacturing facility visible from the showroom.

shops.name: Dandelion Chocolate
shops.description: A bean-to-bar chocolate maker with a factory, café, and education center in the Mission / SoMa border, where visitors can see chocolate being made and sample single-origin bars.

shops.name: Creativity Explored
shops.type: Art nonprofit gallery and gift shop
shops.description: A nonprofit studio and gallery supporting artists with developmental disabilities, selling original artwork, prints, and gifts created by the resident artists in its SoMa program.

shops.name: SOMArts Cultural Center Shop
shops.type: Community arts center with artist merchandise
shops.description: SOMArts hosts rotating exhibitions and events, with artist merchandise and publications available to support the cross-cultural community arts organization's programming.

shops.name: MAC (Modern Appealing Clothing)
shops.description: A respected independent fashion boutique in the Yellow Building in Dogpatch carrying an eclectic mix of avant-garde and accessible designer brands for men and women.

artEntertainment.name: SFMOMA
artEntertainment.description: The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art anchors the SoMa arts district with world-class holdings including the Doris and Donald Fisher Collection, and presents major rotating exhibitions year-round; the Matisse show runs through September 13, and the headline RM x SFMOMA exhibition opens October 3.

artEntertainment.name: Minnesota Street Project
artEntertainment.description: Three converted warehouses in Dogpatch provide affordable, long-term gallery space for independent contemporary art galleries and artists, now including a new permanent Ruth Asawa gallery and Art of Contemporary Africa.

artEntertainment.name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (YBCA)
artEntertainment.description: A cornerstone of the Yerba Buena arts district, YBCA presents contemporary visual art, performance, film, and community programs in galleries and a theater complex adjacent to Yerba Buena Gardens.

artEntertainment.name: SOMArts Cultural Center
artEntertainment.description: SOMArts is a cross-cultural, community-rooted arts organization presenting rotating exhibitions and public events from emerging Bay Area artists, including the 2026 Murphy and Cadogan Contemporary Art Awards Exhibition opening in October.

artEntertainment.name: The Midway
artEntertainment.description: A large-format live music, art, and events venue in Dogpatch with multiple indoor and outdoor spaces hosting concerts, gallery shows, and private events.

artEntertainment.name: Oracle Park
artEntertainment.type: Major league baseball park and event venue
artEntertainment.description: Home of the San Francisco Giants, Oracle Park sits at the edge of SoMa and Mission Bay and hosts concerts and events in addition to baseball, with iconic views of McCovey Cove.
artEntertainment.address: 24 Willie Mays Plaza, San Francisco, CA 94107

artEntertainment.name: Chase Center
artEntertainment.description: The 18,000-seat home of the Golden State Warriors in Mission Bay doubles as one of the Bay Area's premier concert and entertainment venues.

artEntertainment.name: Yerba Buena Gardens Festival (Outdoor Stage)
artEntertainment.description: Running May through November in the open-air lawns of Yerba Buena Gardens, this nonprofit festival presents over 100 free performances of world music, dance, theater, and children's programming.
artEntertainment.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA 94103

artEntertainment.name: Treasure Island Museum
artEntertainment.description: The Treasure Island Museum chronicles the island's history as the site of the 1939 Golden Gate International Exposition and its decades as a Navy base, with archives tours and an annual Swing Dance Benefit fundraiser.

artEntertainment.name: Little Raven Gallery
artEntertainment.description: An intimate SoMa gallery at 1015 Howard Street presenting contemporary works with regular exhibition openings.

gymsRecreation.name: Dogpatch Boulders
gymsRecreation.description: A well-regarded bouldering gym in Dogpatch offering routes for all skill levels from beginner to advanced, with group fitness classes and youth programming.

gymsRecreation.name: YMCA of Greater San Francisco — Dogpatch at Crane Cove

gymsRecreation.name: 3rd Street Boxing Gym
gymsRecreation.description: A fixture of the Dogpatch neighborhood since 2003, offering boxing, kickboxing, and body conditioning classes for all levels near the T-Third Muni stop.

gymsRecreation.name: Fitness SF — SoMa
gymsRecreation.description: A large, airy full-service gym in SoMa with extensive cardio and weight equipment, group fitness classes, and a friendly, knowledgeable staff.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga — Mission Bay
gymsRecreation.description: A Mission Bay location of the popular CorePower Yoga chain, offering a full schedule of heated yoga and sculpt classes near UCSF.

gymsRecreation.name: Bay Padel Dogpatch

gymsRecreation.name: 24 Hour Fitness — Potrero Hill
gymsRecreation.description: A full-service 24-hour gym in Potrero Hill with cardio equipment, free weights, and group fitness classes accessible around the clock.

gymsRecreation.name: Crane Cove Park
gymsRecreation.description: A new waterfront park on the Dogpatch shoreline featuring a public swimming beach, restored historic crane structures, open lawn, and bay views — one of San Francisco's most significant recent park openings.
gymsRecreation.address: 2 Cesar Chavez St, San Francisco, CA 94107

gymsRecreation.name: Bakar Fitness & Recreation Center (UCSF)
gymsRecreation.description: UCSF's state-of-the-art fitness facility at the Mission Bay campus is open to the university community and offers an aquatic center, extensive gym equipment, and group fitness programming.
